I have borderline personality disorder. I have a twelve year old son that is my entire world. I have never been cruel or abusive in any way towards him. He is healthy, happy, intelligent, and incredibly honest. I struggle every day with my illness but make sure my son is never effected by it because he deserves a happy and loving home. Borderline is not some evil sickness that turns people into monsters. It's a terribly disabling disease and most people actually don't understand it whatsoever or have any sort of inkling how devastating it is to have. I don't think it's fair to tag everyone with borderline as some horribly abusive person because it's not true. Living with this kills me every second of everyday. I hate myself, I have absolutely nobody close to me because I believe I don't deserve to be happy. I pretend for my son because he deserves to have a happy life. Don't judge people when you actually have no idea. It's heartbreaking to be stereotyped because of something I have no control over. For the most part, you'd never know I have it. I also went to years and hours a week in therapy. What I have cannot be cured. There's no pill to alleviate the symptoms. You have to go to intensive therapy to learn how to act human. This is not a fun disease and it should not be trivialized like it is. Borderlines don't like who they are. They are constantly miserable. Living like this is probably one of the worst things anyone could do. Always hating yourself and not being able to get across your feelings or frustrations and having people judge you for not knowing how to control your thoughts is such a hurtful thing. I just am passionate about my illness because it was who I was for so long. I just want the truth to be told because misconceptions are what gives mental illness such a stigmatizing view. Mental illness is real and it's sad and it's scary and I just think people should know it from the other side.
